start.title: Three steps
start.guide: Everything is in the <guide>self-hosting guide</guide>. Prebuilt images are published with the v0.4.0-alpha release; the <images>release images guide</images> explains how to use them.

0.title: Check you can run it
0.body: You need a machine that runs Docker and Docker Compose, with plenty of free memory and disk. The guide lists the exact needs.

1.title: Add your settings
1.body: Copy the sample settings file and fill in the required secrets. You add your AI provider keys in the dashboard after you sign in.

2.title: Start it and open the dashboard
2.body: The guide walks through each step and what to do when something does not start.

licence.title: The licence in plain words
licence.p1: ReelBolt is released under AGPL-3.0. Running it for yourself or your team is free, and you do not have to publish anything. If you change it and let other people use your version over a network, you must share your changes under the same licence. This is a summary, not legal advice, so read the <licence>licence text</licence> if it matters to you.
licence.p2: If that does not suit you, because you want to embed ReelBolt in a product you sell, run a changed version as a service without publishing it, or need contractual terms such as a warranty or support, there is a commercial licence. Write to <mail>legal@reelbolt.ai</mail> or read the <commercial>commercial licence details</commercial>.
licence.p3: The video render engine, Remotion, is not part of our licence and is not open source. It is source-available under its own terms, and when you self-host you are its licensee. Its free licence covers individuals, for-profit organisations of up to three people, non-profits and anyone evaluating it. Larger organisations need a Company License. The Remotion team has confirmed ReelBolt’s own use of Remotion. Read the terms at <remotion>remotion.dev/docs/license</remotion>.
licence.p4: The ReelBolt name and logo are reserved by the project owner, Tommaso Celano. You can say you run ReelBolt, but a fork needs its own name. The details are in <trademark>trademark policy</trademark>.

contribute.title: Send a fix, a step or an idea
contribute.p1: You sign a contributor licence agreement once, with a single sentence on your first pull request, and you keep the copyright on what you write. The <guide>contributing guide</guide> explains the rest. Bugs and questions go to the <issues>issue list</issues>.

0.a: The software is free to run under AGPL-3.0. You pay for your own server and for the AI services you connect.

1.q: What is the difference from the hosted version?
1.a: Hosted means no setup, no provider accounts to open and support by plan. Self-hosting means you run everything yourself and get community help through GitHub issues.

2.q: Can I use it at work?
2.a: Yes. Running it for your own team needs nothing from us. The video render engine has its own licence, and you hold it for your install. A company above the free size limit needs a Company License from the engine’s authors. If you want to embed ReelBolt in a product you sell, or run a changed version as a service without publishing your changes, ask us about a commercial licence at legal@reelbolt.ai.

3.a: It is an early alpha and this is the first open-source release, so expect rough edges and changes between versions. If you need something steady today, the hosted service is the safer path.

4.a: Yes. You sign a contributor licence agreement once, with a single sentence on your first pull request, and you keep the copyright on what you write. The contributing guide and the issue list on GitHub are the place to start.
